claim: MCAT is an enzyme involved in mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS).
source: Malonyl-CoA-acyl carrier protein transacylase (MCAT) is an enzyme involved in mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) and catalyzes the transfer of the malonyl moiety of malonyl-CoA to the mitochondrial acyl carrier protein (ACP).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction as established knowledge about MCAT function.

claim: MCAT catalyzes the transfer of the malonyl moiety of malonyl-CoA to the mitochondrial acyl carrier protein (ACP).
source: Malonyl-CoA-acyl carrier protein transacylase (MCAT) is an enzyme involved in mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) and catalyzes the transfer of the malonyl moiety of malonyl-CoA to the mitochondrial acyl carrier protein (ACP).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as established knowledge about MCAT's catalytic function.

claim: Loss-of-function of mtFAS genes, including Mcat, is associated with severe loss of electron transport chain (ETC) complexes in mouse immortalized skeletal myoblasts.
source: Previously, we showed that loss-of-function of mtFAS genes, including Mcat, is associated with severe loss of electron transport chain (ETC) complexes in mouse immortalized skeletal myoblasts (Nowinski et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work by Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: A proband presented with hypotonia, failure to thrive, nystagmus, and abnormal brain MRI findings.
source: Here, we report a proband presenting with hypotonia, failure to thrive, nystagmus, and abnormal brain MRI findings.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation reported in the abstract.

claim: Biallelic variants in MCAT were identified in the proband using whole exome sequencing.
source: Using whole exome sequencing, we identified biallelic variants in MCAT.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from whole exome sequencing described in the manuscript.

claim: Protein levels for NDUFB8 and COXII were markedly reduced in lymphoblasts and fibroblasts from the proband.
source: Protein levels for NDUFB8 and COXII, subunits of complex I and IV respectively, were markedly reduced in lymphoblasts and fibroblasts, as well as SDHB for complex II in fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2.

claim: SDHB protein levels were markedly reduced in fibroblasts from the proband.
source: Protein levels for NDUFB8 and COXII, subunits of complex I and IV respectively, were markedly reduced in lymphoblasts and fibroblasts, as well as SDHB for complex II in fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: ETC enzyme activities were decreased in parallel with reduced protein levels in the proband.
source: ETC enzyme activities were decreased in parallel.
evidence: This is supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: Re-expression of wild-type MCAT rescued the phenotype in patient fibroblasts.
source: Re-expression of wild-type MCAT rescued the phenotype in patient fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: This is the first report of a patient with MCAT pathogenic variants and combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.
source: This is the first report of a patient with MCAT pathogenic variants and combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the report, based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: MCAT acts at the second step of mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis whereby malonyl-CoA is used to generate malonyl-acyl carrier protein (ACP).
source: MCAT acts at the second step of mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) whereby malonyl-CoA is used to generate malonyl-acyl carrier protein (ACP) (Hiltunen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hiltunen et al., 2009.

claim: Octanoate, the precursor for the co-factor lipoate, is thought to be the main product of the mtFAS system.
source: Octanoate, the precursor for the co-factor lipoate, is thought to be the main product of the mtFAS system.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mtFAS system.

claim: Lipoylation is necessary for the activity of the pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDHc), 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase (OGDHc), branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase (BCKDHc), and 2-oxoadipate dehydrogenase complexes, and the glycine cleavage system.
source: Lipoylation is necessary for the activity of the pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDHc), 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase (OGDHc), branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase (BCKDHc), and 2-oxoadipate dehydrogenase complexes, and the glycine cleavage system (Solmonson and DeBerardinis, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Solmonson and DeBerardinis, 2018.

claim: A mouse model with reduced Mcat expression displays decreased physical activity, reduced muscle strength, and premature aging with a reduced life span.
source: A mouse model with reduced Mcat expression displays decreased physical activity, reduced muscle strength, and premature aging with a reduced life span.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2012.

claim: Mice with reduced Mcat expression have elevated skeletal muscle lactate, blood lactate, and ketone bodies.
source: Additionally, these animals have elevated skeletal muscle lactate, blood lactate, and ketone bodies, and have lipoylation defects in OGDHc, PDHc, and BCKDHc.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2012.

claim: Mice with reduced Mcat expression have lipoylation defects in OGDHc, PDHc, and BCKDHc.
source: Additionally, these animals have elevated skeletal muscle lactate, blood lactate, and ketone bodies, and have lipoylation defects in OGDHc, PDHc, and BCKDHc.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2012.

claim: The mouse phenotype with reduced Mcat expression is due primarily to decreased generation of octanoate, leading to decreased lipoylation of PDHc and OGDHc and decreased flux through the citric acid cycle with subsequent disruption of energy metabolism.
source: The authors postulated that the mouse phenotype is due primarily to decreased generation of octanoate, leading to decreased lipoylation of PDHc and OGDHc and decreased flux through the citric acid cycle with subsequent disruption of energy metabolism (Smith et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from Smith et al., 2012, cited in the manuscript.

claim: The mitochondrial ACP encoded by NDUFAB1 has been shown to be essential for complex I assembly.
source: Although MCAT has not been demonstrated to have a role in oxidative phosphorylation, the mitochondrial ACP encoded by NDUFAB1 has been shown to be essential for complex I assembly (Stroud et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stroud et al., 2016.

claim: Hypomorphic Mcat clones have a 30–40% decreased basal respiration rate compared to controls.
source: These hypomorphic Mcat clones have a 30–40% decreased basal respiration rate compared to controls, which is explained by markedly decreased levels of fully assembled complexes I, II, and IV.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: Hypomorphic Mcat clones have markedly decreased levels of fully assembled complexes I, II, and IV.
source: These hypomorphic Mcat clones have a 30–40% decreased basal respiration rate compared to controls, which is explained by markedly decreased levels of fully assembled complexes I, II, and IV.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: Metabolomics and carbon-labeling studies are consistent with decreased function of the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation in hypomorphic Mcat mutant cells.
source: Metabolomics and carbon-labeling studies are all consistent with decreased function of the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation in the hypomorphic Mcat mutant cells (Nowinski et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: The role of mtFAS extends beyond protein lipoylation and includes a crucial role in the maintenance of electron transport chain (ETC) activity.
source: This work demonstrates that the role of mtFAS extends beyond protein lipoylation and includes a crucial role in the maintenance of electron transport chain (ETC) activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the work of Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: The proband is a 2-year-old boy born prematurely with a past medical history notable for failure to thrive and global developmental delay.
source: A 2-year-old boy, born prematurely, with a past medical history notable for failure to thrive and global developmental delay presented for genetics evaluation.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: The proband's birth weight was 1.106 kg.
source: Birth weight was 1.106 kg.
evidence: This is a direct clinical measurement from the case presentation.

claim: The patient was hospitalized in the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory support and was discharged home at 7 weeks.
source: The patient was hospitalized in the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory support (oxygen via nasal cannula) and was discharged home at 7 weeks.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: At 8 months of age, the patient was noted to have esotropia and horizontal jerk nystagmus that decreased with convergence.
source: The patient was being followed by ophthalmology for retinopathy of prematurity and at 8 months of age was noted to have esotropia and horizontal jerk nystagmus that decreased with convergence.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: At 19 months, the patient was noted to have new-onset vertical nystagmus.
source: He was prescribed eye patching resulting in some improvement of the esotropia, but at 19 months was noted to have new-onset vertical nystagmus.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: Brain MRI at 21 months showed bilaterally symmetrical increase in signal intensity on T2- and T2 FLAIR-weighted sequences in the dorsal medulla, periaqueductal gray matter, substantia nigra, medial hypothalamus, and habenular nuclei.
source: A brain MRI completed at 21 months was notable for bilaterally symmetrical increase in signal intensity on T2- and T2 FLAIR (fluid attenuated inversion recovery)-weighted sequences in the dorsal medulla, periaqueductal gray matter, substantia nigra, medial hypothalamus, and habenular nuclei.
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from the case presentation.

claim: Brain MRI at 21 months showed two asymmetric foci in the subcortical white matter of the cerebellar hemispheres.
source: There were two asymmetric foci in the subcortical white matter of the cerebellar hemispheres.
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from the case presentation.

claim: At 2 years of age, the patient could say approximately two to three words, had no two-word phrases, and could not walk independently.
source: Developmentally, at 2 years of age the patient could say approximately two to three words, had no two-word phrases, and could not walk independently.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: At 2 years of age, the patient's head circumference was at the 0.4 percentile (Z=−2.59).
source: On exam, his head circumference was at the 0.4 percentile (Z=−2.59), height was at the 0.46 percentile (Z=−2.61), and weight was at the <0.01 percentile (Z=−3.73).
evidence: This is a direct clinical measurement from the case presentation.

claim: At 2 years of age, the patient's height was at the 0.46 percentile (Z=−2.61).
source: On exam, his head circumference was at the 0.4 percentile (Z=−2.59), height was at the 0.46 percentile (Z=−2.61), and weight was at the <0.01 percentile (Z=−3.73).
evidence: This is a direct clinical measurement from the case presentation.

claim: At 2 years of age, the patient's weight was at the <0.01 percentile (Z=−3.73).
source: On exam, his head circumference was at the 0.4 percentile (Z=−2.59), height was at the 0.46 percentile (Z=−2.61), and weight was at the <0.01 percentile (Z=−3.73).
evidence: This is a direct clinical measurement from the case presentation.

claim: The patient had plagiocephaly with sagittal suture prominence.
source: He had plagiocephaly with sagittal suture prominence, but was otherwise nondysmorphic.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: Vertical and horizontal nystagmus were present in the patient.
source: Vertical and horizontal nystagmus were present.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: Neurological exam was notable for truncal and peripheral hypotonia, decreased muscle mass, and brisk reflexes.
source: Neurological exam was notable for truncal and peripheral hypotonia, decreased muscle mass, and brisk reflexes.
evidence: This is a direct clinical observation from the case presentation.

claim: Serum creatine kinase, blood lactate, pyruvate, ammonia, acylcarnitine profile, plasma amino acids, and urine organic acids were normal in the patient.
source: Serum creatine kinase, blood lactate, pyruvate, ammonia, acylcarnitine profile, plasma amino acids, and urine organic acids were normal.
evidence: This is a direct clinical laboratory observation from the case presentation.

claim: Repeat brain MRI at 3 years 3 months showed substantially increased signal intensity and extent of involvement at the same sites as the earlier MRI.
source: Repeat brain MRI at 3 years 3 months showed substantially increased signal intensity and extent of involvement at the same sites, with no edema, no mass effect, and no abnormal contrast enhancement at any site (Figure 1A–F; Naidich and Duvernoy, 2009; Standring, 2020).
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from the case presentation, with reference to Figure 1.

claim: No new sites of involvement were identified on repeat brain MRI at 3 years 3 months.
source: No new sites of involvement were identified.
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from the case presentation.

claim: Brain MR spectroscopy at short TE was normal within the right thalamus and left subcortical white matter.
source: Brain MR spectroscopy at short TE was normal within the right thalamus and left subcortical white matter.
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from the case presentation.

claim: Chromosomal microarray revealed no pathogenic copy number variation.
source: Chromosomal microarray revealed no pathogenic copy number variation, but absence of heterozygosity of unknown clinical significance totaling 32.2 Mb was detected.
evidence: This is a direct genetic testing result from the case presentation.

claim: Chromosomal microarray detected absence of heterozygosity of unknown clinical significance totaling 32.2 Mb.
source: Chromosomal microarray revealed no pathogenic copy number variation, but absence of heterozygosity of unknown clinical significance totaling 32.2 Mb was detected.
evidence: This is a direct genetic testing result from the case presentation.

claim: The proband has an older sibling who was born with cleft lip and died at a year of age from a choking episode.
source: Family history was significant for an older sibling born with cleft lip, who died at a year of age from a choking episode.
evidence: This is a direct family history observation from the case presentation.

claim: Visual symptoms were not seen in the proband's older sibling.
source: Visual symptoms were not seen in this sibling.
evidence: This is a direct family history observation from the case presentation.

claim: The proband has two younger siblings who are healthy and have normal development.
source: The proband has two younger siblings who are healthy and have normal development.
evidence: This is a direct family history observation from the case presentation.

claim: Both parents are from the same region of Mexico.
source: Family history was otherwise non-contributory, and while both parents are from the same region of Mexico, consanguinity was denied.
evidence: This is a direct family history observation from the case presentation.

claim: Consanguinity was denied by the parents.
source: Family history was otherwise non-contributory, and while both parents are from the same region of Mexico, consanguinity was denied.
evidence: This is a direct family history observation from the case presentation.

claim: A homozygous variant in MCAT c.812T>C; p.T271I was identified in the proband by whole exome sequencing.
source: By whole exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous variant in MCAT c.812T>C; p.T271I (rs760294168; NM_173467.4) in the proband, which was heterozygous in both parents consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
evidence: This is supported by whole exome sequencing data.

claim: The MCAT variant c.812T>C; p.T271I was heterozygous in both parents.
source: By whole exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous variant in MCAT c.812T>C; p.T271I (rs760294168; NM_173467.4) in the proband, which was heterozygous in both parents consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
evidence: This is supported by whole exome sequencing data.

claim: The MCAT variant c.812T>C; p.T271I is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
source: By whole exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous variant in MCAT c.812T>C; p.T271I (rs760294168; NM_173467.4) in the proband, which was heterozygous in both parents consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genetic data showing homozygosity in the proband and heterozygosity in both parents.

claim: The MCAT variant p.T271I has a high CADD score of 28.9.
source: This variant had a high CADD score of 28.9, is predicted to be damaging and probably damaging by SIFT and PolyPhen-2, respectively, and is in gnomAD at very low frequency (2/251,156 alleles; no homozygotes reported).
evidence: This is supported by computational prediction tools.

claim: The MCAT variant p.T271I is predicted to be damaging by SIFT.
source: This variant had a high CADD score of 28.9, is predicted to be damaging and probably damaging by SIFT and PolyPhen-2, respectively, and is in gnomAD at very low frequency (2/251,156 alleles; no homozygotes reported).
evidence: This is supported by computational prediction tools.

claim: The MCAT variant p.T271I is predicted to be probably damaging by PolyPhen-2.
source: This variant had a high CADD score of 28.9, is predicted to be damaging and probably damaging by SIFT and PolyPhen-2, respectively, and is in gnomAD at very low frequency (2/251,156 alleles; no homozygotes reported).
evidence: This is supported by computational prediction tools.

claim: The MCAT variant p.T271I is in gnomAD at very low frequency (2/251,156 alleles; no homozygotes reported).
source: This variant had a high CADD score of 28.9, is predicted to be damaging and probably damaging by SIFT and PolyPhen-2, respectively, and is in gnomAD at very low frequency (2/251,156 alleles; no homozygotes reported).
evidence: This is supported by population frequency data from gnomAD.

claim: The residue p.T271 in MCAT is highly conserved across species, from human to Xenopus and zebrafish.
source: In addition, p.T271 is highly conserved across species, from human to Xenopus and zebrafish.
evidence: This is supported by evolutionary conservation analysis.

claim: Immunoblot analysis revealed a decreased protein level for MCAT in lymphoblasts from the proband.
source: In lymphoblasts, immunoblot analysis revealed a decreased protein level for MCAT as well as NDUFB8 and COXII, which are selected subunits of complex I and IV, respectively (Figure 2A–B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Immunoblot analysis revealed decreased protein levels for NDUFB8 and COXII in lymphoblasts from the proband.
source: In lymphoblasts, immunoblot analysis revealed a decreased protein level for MCAT as well as NDUFB8 and COXII, which are selected subunits of complex I and IV, respectively (Figure 2A–B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Immunoblot analysis revealed decreased protein levels for NDUFB8, SDHB, UQCRC2, and COXII in fibroblasts from the proband.
source: In fibroblasts, immunoblot analysis revealed decreased protein levels for NDUFB8, SDHB, UQCRC2, and COXII which are selected subunits of complexes I, II, III, and IV, respectively (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Respiratory chain enzyme activities for complexes I, II, and IV were decreased in the proband's fibroblasts.
source: Respiratory chain enzyme activities were evaluated in the proband's fibroblasts and revealed decreased activities for complexes I, II, and IV (Table 1; Rodenburg, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by enzyme activity measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: ETC components assemble into respiratory supercomplexes composed of complexes I, III, and IV in varying stoichiometries in mammals.
source: In mammals, ETC components assemble into respiratory supercomplexes composed of complexes I, III, and IV in varying stoichiometries (Letts et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Letts et al., 2016.

claim: Intact, fully assembled complex I-containing supercomplexes were decreased in abundance in fibroblasts from the patient by blue-native PAGE.
source: Intact, fully assembled complex I-containing supercomplexes and complex IV-containing supercomplexes were decreased in abundance in fibroblasts from the patient by blue-native PAGE (BN-PAGE), similar to what we observed in SDS-PAGE analysis.
evidence: This is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Intact, fully assembled complex IV-containing supercomplexes were decreased in abundance in fibroblasts from the patient by blue-native PAGE.
source: Intact, fully assembled complex I-containing supercomplexes and complex IV-containing supercomplexes were decreased in abundance in fibroblasts from the patient by blue-native PAGE (BN-PAGE), similar to what we observed in SDS-PAGE analysis.
evidence: This is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The complex III-containing supercomplexes appeared decreased in abundance in patient fibroblasts.
source: The complex III-containing supercomplexes also appeared decreased in abundance in patient fibroblasts, although this can likely be attributed to the observed decreases in complexes I and IV, especially in light of no measured difference in complex III activity.
evidence: This is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The decrease in complex III-containing supercomplexes can likely be attributed to the observed decreases in complexes I and IV.
source: The complex III-containing supercomplexes also appeared decreased in abundance in patient fibroblasts, although this can likely be attributed to the observed decreases in complexes I and IV, especially in light of no measured difference in complex III activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that complex III activity was normal while complexes I and IV were decreased.

claim: Re-expression of MCAT (+hMCAT) partially rescued mitochondrial phenotypes in the patient cells.
source: Re-expression of MCAT (+hMCAT), but not a mitochondrially targeted GFP construct (+mtGFP), partially rescued these mitochondrial phenotypes in the patient cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 3.

claim: A mitochondrially targeted GFP construct (+mtGFP) did not rescue mitochondrial phenotypes in the patient cells.
source: Re-expression of MCAT (+hMCAT), but not a mitochondrially targeted GFP construct (+mtGFP), partially rescued these mitochondrial phenotypes in the patient cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Immunoblot analysis with an anti-lipoic acid antibody noted no change in lipoylation in the proband's lymphoblasts compared to control samples.
source: To assess lipoylation, we performed immunoblot analysis in lymphoblasts with an anti-lipoic acid antibody and noted no change in the proband compared to control samples (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: OGDHc activity was normal in the proband's lymphoblasts compared to controls.
source: We also measured OGDHc activity in lymphoblasts and noted no deficits in the proband compared to controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by enzyme activity data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Lactate is elevated in patient fibroblasts compared to control fibroblast lines.
source: This revealed that lactate is elevated in the patient cells, but metabolites related to other 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes including 2-oxoglutarate and 2-oxoadipate were within the range of normal, consistent with the lack of a deficiency in lipoylation and normal OGDHc activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Metabolites related to other 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes including 2-oxoglutarate and 2-oxoadipate were within the range of normal in patient fibroblasts.
source: This revealed that lactate is elevated in the patient cells, but metabolites related to other 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes including 2-oxoglutarate and 2-oxoadipate were within the range of normal, consistent with the lack of a deficiency in lipoylation and normal OGDHc activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Re-expression of wild-type and p.T271I human MCAT rescued protein lipoylation in hypomorphic Mcat mutant C2C12 cells.
source: Re-expression of wild-type and p.T271I human MCAT rescued protein lipoylation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The effect of re-expression of wild-type and p.T271I human MCAT on the expression of NDUFA9, a complex I subunit, was more variable in hypomorphic Mcat mutant C2C12 cells.
source: The effect on the expression of NDUFA9, a complex I subunit, was more variable (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mcat hypomorphic mutant C2C12 exhibited significantly decreased basal and maximal respiration rates compared to controls.
source: In comparison to controls, Mcat hypomorphic mutant C2C12 exhibited significantly decreased basal and maximal respiration rates, as previously described (Figure 4B and C; Nowinski et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by Seahorse respiration data shown in Figure 4B and C, and a citation to Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: Expression of a mitochondrially targeted DSRed construct (mtDSRed) minimally affected respiration in the Mcat mutant C2C12 cells.
source: Expression of a mitochondrially targeted DSRed construct (mtDSRed) minimally affected respiration in the Mcat mutant cells, while expression of wild-type human MCAT fully rescued both basal and maximal respiration rates.
evidence: This is supported by Seahorse respiration data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Expression of wild-type human MCAT fully rescued both basal and maximal respiration rates in Mcat mutant C2C12 cells.
source: Expression of a mitochondrially targeted DSRed construct (mtDSRed) minimally affected respiration in the Mcat mutant cells, while expression of wild-type human MCAT fully rescued both basal and maximal respiration rates.
evidence: This is supported by Seahorse respiration data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Expression of the p.T271I mutant only partially rescued respiration in Mcat mutant C2C12 cells.
source: In contrast, expression of the p.T271I mutant only partially rescued respiration (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by Seahorse respiration data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The homozygous variant in MCAT c.812T>C; p.T271I leads to combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.
source: Taken together, we demonstrate that the homozygous variant in MCAT c.812T>C; p.T271I leads to combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The patient did not have a lipoylation defect noted in lymphoblasts.
source: Interestingly, although MCAT plays a key role in the mtFAS system, which generates octanoate, the precursor for lipoate, our patient did not have a lipoylation defect noted in lymphoblasts and had normal OGDHc activity in lymphoblasts (Mayr et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot and enzyme activity data.

claim: The patient had normal OGDHc activity in lymphoblasts.
source: Interestingly, although MCAT plays a key role in the mtFAS system, which generates octanoate, the precursor for lipoate, our patient did not have a lipoylation defect noted in lymphoblasts and had normal OGDHc activity in lymphoblasts (Mayr et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by enzyme activity data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Biochemical findings that would indicate a lipoate deficiency such as lactic acidemia, elevated urine 2-oxoglutarate, and elevated blood glycine were absent in the patient.
source: Consistently, other biochemical findings that would indicate a lipoate deficiency such as lactic acidemia, elevated urine 2-oxoglutarate, and elevated blood glycine were absent.
evidence: This is supported by clinical laboratory data from the case presentation.

claim: This finding is unique relative to other, previously described pathogenic mtFAS mutations, which usually display both lipoylation and ETC defects.
source: This finding is unique relative to other, previously described pathogenic mtFAS mutations, which usually display both lipoylation and ETC defects (Heimer et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior literature, supported by citations to Heimer et al., 2016 and Liu et al., 2021.

claim: The decoupling of mtFAS endpoints may be a result of substrate limitation due to the less functional MCAT mutant decreasing available malonyl-ACP.
source: We hypothesize that this decoupling of mtFAS endpoints may be a result of substrate limitation. Because MCAT supplies malonyl-ACP which is necessary to extend acyl chains, this less functional MCAT mutant may decrease the available malonyl-ACP and therefore preference the pathway toward shorter chain products (like lipoic acid) over the longer acyl chains that are required for LYRM binding and ETC assembly.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors to explain their observations.

claim: Double homozygous mutations in MCAT (p.L81R and p.R212W) were identified in a consanguineous Chinese family with isolated, progressive autosomal recessive optic neuropathy.
source: Recently, double homozygous mutations in MCAT (p.L81R and p.R212W) were identified in a consanguineous Chinese family with isolated, progressive autosomal recessive optic neuropathy.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2020.

claim: Patients with double homozygous MCAT mutations (p.L81R and p.R212W) were otherwise healthy, had normal motor function, and brain MR imaging revealed only bilateral thinning of the optic nerve.
source: These patients were otherwise healthy, had normal motor function, and brain MR imaging revealed only bilateral thinning of the optic nerve.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2020.

claim: Overexpression of L81R MCAT or double mutant L81R/R212W MCAT led to decreased COX4 expression in the mitochondria in HEK293T cells.
source: Overexpression of L81R MCAT or double mutant L81R/R212W MCAT led to decreased COX4 expression in the mitochondria in HEK293T cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2020.

claim: MCAT L81R and R212W variants only affect retinal ganglion cell axon maintenance.
source: The authors hypothesize that MCAT L81R and R212W variants only affect retinal ganglion cell axon maintenance (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from Li et al., 2020, cited in the manuscript.

claim: The patient with the homozygous MCAT p.T271I pathogenic variant exhibits more severe mitochondrial disease characterized by multi-system involvement.
source: Our patient with the homozygous MCAT p.T271I pathogenic variant exhibits more severe mitochondrial disease characterized by multi-system involvement.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current patient and previously reported patients, based on clinical observations.

claim: The MCAT mutation p.T271I is located adjacent to the active site.
source: The identified mutation, c.812T>C; p.T271I, is located adjacent to the active site, and likely affects both the stability and catalytic activity of the enzyme (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural modeling shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The MCAT mutation p.T271I likely affects both the stability and catalytic activity of the enzyme.
source: The identified mutation, c.812T>C; p.T271I, is located adjacent to the active site, and likely affects both the stability and catalytic activity of the enzyme (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural modeling shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Defects in complexes I, II, and IV were noted in fibroblasts based on enzyme activity assays.
source: Defects in complexes I, II, and IV were noted in fibroblasts based on enzyme activity assays and immunoblotting for individual subunits of the complexes.
evidence: This is supported by enzyme activity data shown in Table 1.

claim: Defects in complexes I, II, and IV were noted in fibroblasts based on immunoblotting for individual subunits of the complexes.
source: Defects in complexes I, II, and IV were noted in fibroblasts based on enzyme activity assays and immunoblotting for individual subunits of the complexes.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Subunits of complexes I and IV were decreased in lymphoblasts from the proband.
source: Additionally, subunits of complexes I and IV were also decreased in lymphoblasts.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: BN-PAGE revealed that intact and fully assembled supercomplexes I, III, and IV were decreased in abundance in patient fibroblasts.
source: BN-PAGE revealed that intact and fully assembled supercomplexes I, III, and IV were decreased in abundance in patient fibroblasts.
evidence: This is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Wild-type MCAT led to increased abundance of supercomplexes I, III, and IV in patient fibroblasts, proving causality of the MCAT variant.
source: Wild-type MCAT led to increased abundance of each of these three complexes proving causality of the MCAT variant.
evidence: This is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 3, demonstrating rescue of the phenotype.

claim: The T235 residue in the crystal structure corresponds to the residue at the site of the T271I mutation.
source: The T235 residue in the crystal structure corresponds to the residue at the site of the T271I mutation.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The T271I mutation occurs one residue away from the active site histidine (H234).
source: This mutation occurs one residue away from the active site histidine (H234) and is located in a semi-structured region between the end of an alpha helix and a linker region between the alpha helix and a series of beta sheets.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: In the wild-type protein, the T235 residue makes several contacts with surrounding residues.
source: In the wild-type protein, the T235 residue makes several contacts with surrounding residues.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The mutation of threonine to isoleucine results in a loss of polar contacts with A232 and L238 due to a loss of the hydroxyl moiety.
source: The mutation of threonine to isoleucine results in a loss of polar contacts with A232 and L238 due to a loss of the hydroxyl moiety.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The loss of polar contacts likely reduces the structure of the end of the alpha helix and may generate additional flexibility of the linker region.
source: This likely reduces the structure of the end of the alpha helix and may generate additional flexibility of the linker region.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural modeling shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The proximity of the T271I mutation to the active site may suggest a negative impact on catalytic efficiency.
source: Although the mutant protein shows maintenance of a contact between the active site histidine and another active site residue (S117), the proximity of this mutation to the active site may suggest a negative impact on catalytic efficiency.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural modeling shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: 96% of the exome was covered at ≥10× in whole exome sequencing.
source: Sequence reads were independently mapped to the reference genome (hg19) with BWA-MEM and further processed using the GATK Best Practices workflows (Li and Durbin, 2009; Van der Auwera et al., 2013; McKenna et al., 2010); 96% of the exome was covered at ≥10×.
evidence: This is a quality metric from the whole exome sequencing analysis.

claim: A total of 102,052 total variants in 17,924 genes were identified in the three samples by whole exome sequencing.
source: A total of 102,052 total variants in 17,924 genes were identified in the three samples.
evidence: This is a result from the whole exome sequencing analysis.

claim: The filtering strategy for whole exome sequencing resulted in the identification of 21 variants in 20 genes.
source: This filtering strategy resulted in the identification of 21 variants in 20 genes.
evidence: This is a result from the whole exome sequencing analysis.

claim: Hypomorphic Mcat C2C12 cell lines display a roughly 90% reduction in MCAT expression.
source: These cells display a roughly 90% reduction in MCAT expression, and similar to the proband fibroblasts have defects in assembly and stability of ETC complexes I, II, and IV.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: Hypomorphic Mcat C2C12 cell lines have defects in assembly and stability of ETC complexes I, II, and IV.
source: These cells display a roughly 90% reduction in MCAT expression, and similar to the proband fibroblasts have defects in assembly and stability of ETC complexes I, II, and IV.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: Hypomorphic Mcat C2C12 lines have undetectable protein lipoylation by western blot.
source: However, the hypomorphic Mcat C2C12 lines also have undetectable protein lipoylation by western blot (Nowinski et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nowinski et al., 2020.

claim: Brain MRI sections through the medulla and mid pons demonstrate well-defined, symmetrical signal increase in the central tegmental tracts and the nuclei prepositus hypoglossi.
source: (A–B) Sections through the brainstem and cerebellum. Sections through the medulla (A) and mid pons (B) demonstrate well-defined, symmetrical signal increase in the central tegmental tracts (1) and the nuclei prepositus hypoglossi (2) with very limited, slightly asymmetrical involvement of the white matter of both cerebellar hemispheres (3).
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from Figure 1.

claim: Brain MRI sections through the medulla and mid pons show very limited, slightly asymmetrical involvement of the white matter of both cerebellar hemispheres.
source: (A–B) Sections through the brainstem and cerebellum. Sections through the medulla (A) and mid pons (B) demonstrate well-defined, symmetrical signal increase in the central tegmental tracts (1) and the nuclei prepositus hypoglossi (2) with very limited, slightly asymmetrical involvement of the white matter of both cerebellar hemispheres (3).
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from Figure 1.

claim: Brain MRI sections through the midbrain display intense symmetrical increase in signal in the tectum, peri-aqueductal gray matter, substantia nigra, and medial hypothalamus.
source: (C–D) Sections through the midbrain display intense symmetrical increase in signal in the tectum (4), peri-aqueductal gray matter (5), substantia nigra (6), and medial hypothalamus (7).
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from Figure 1.

claim: The mammillary bodies are spared on brain MRI.
source: The mammillary bodies (8) are spared.
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from Figure 1.

claim: Brain MRI sections through the hypothalamus and thalamus display intense symmetrical increase in signal in the medial thalamus, anteromedial thalamus, and habenular nuclei.
source: (E–F) Sections through the hypothalamus (E) and thalamus (F) display intense symmetrical increase in signal in the medial thalamus (9), anteromedial thalamus (10), and habenular nuclei (11), with sparing of the low signal mammillothalamic tracts (12) and anterior columns of the fornix (13).
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from Figure 1.

claim: The mammillothalamic tracts and anterior columns of the fornix are spared on brain MRI.
source: (E–F) Sections through the hypothalamus (E) and thalamus (F) display intense symmetrical increase in signal in the medial thalamus (9), anteromedial thalamus (10), and habenular nuclei (11), with sparing of the low signal mammillothalamic tracts (12) and anterior columns of the fornix (13).
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from Figure 1.

claim: No abnormal signal was identified in any other portions of the brain on MRI.
source: No abnormal signal was identified in any other portions of the brain.
evidence: This is a direct imaging observation from Figure 1.
